title: TST check for nan and inf + single sample for metrics cl…
description:
Quite interesting that the clustering metrics were accepting non finite input.
@jnothman Do you think about any particular reason to be that much permissive?

comments.author: glemaitre
comments.body:
I will still have one test failing:

https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/master/sklearn/metrics/cluster/tests/test_supervised.py#L51

Does it make sense to have this test. Why the metric should return 1.0 on some empty arrays?

comments.author: glemaitre
comments.body: @amueller Do you know the reason that an empty cluster give the best score?

comments.author: amueller
comments.body: @glemaitre can you please elaborate / give more context?

comments.author: glemaitre
comments.body:
> @glemaitre can you please elaborate / give more context?

From what I recall, there is a failing test `test_perfect_matches` enforcing:
`assert score_func([], []) == 1.0`

The question is: is it making sense that supervised metric for clustering would return a perfect match when a cluster is an empty cluster.

comments.author: jnothman
comments.body:
I think scoring an empty clustering as a perfect clustering makes sense if
any clustering of a single point is a perfect clustering. We could return
NaN instead.

comments.author: glemaitre
comments.body:
ping @rth 

I think that we could merge this one.

comments.author: rth
comments.body:
> is it making sense that supervised metric for clustering would return a perfect match when a cluster is an empty cluster.

I have no idea what the score should be for an empty cluster, but I still wonder if we should error or not with 0 samples.

+        invalids = [([0, 1], [np.inf, np.inf]),

review_comments.author: jnothman
review_comments.body: I don't consider this a user-facing change

review_comments.author: glemaitre
review_comments.body: @amueller note that the test can pass if I allow for 0 sample. I think it was more a general question (but this is a long time ago).

review_comments.author: rth
review_comments.body: That removes the check about the potential second dimension though? Not sure if it matters...

review_comments.author: rth
review_comments.body:
```suggestion
    for i, j in [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]:
```

more explicit..

review_comments.author: rth
review_comments.body:
Everything below this line is strictly identical in both `if` branches. Only `invalids` and metric needs to be defined there I think?

Or rather,
```py
for args in invalids:
    metric(*args)
```
as it's confusing to see `metric(y_true, y_score)` for unsupervised ones.
